Elara Dawn — Album 8.5: Elara Dawn

The Red Woman

"The Red Woman at the table"

[Intro — Elara watching through Illuminate, the room comes into focus] She is still in the field But the sight takes her somewhere else

A room Lit red by torchlight Full of people leaning forward

And one leaning back

[Verse 1 — the room, everyone speaking at once] The Seven are already standing Before the Red Woman has sat down The Riders have their maps unrolled Before the meeting has been called

The priest is at the altar corner Murmuring the blessing early The council has its list of grievances Already in the proper order

And every voice agrees

Now

Now is the moment

The purple woman is distracted The south is overextended The light is on our side And now

Now

They are all so certain In the particular way that people are certain when they want what certainty allows

[Pre-Chorus] And then

One person in the room Is not speaking

One person in the room Is watching every person who is speaking

Her eyes move like a compass Finding north in each of them

And north in each of them is not Leara

[Chorus] The Red Woman at the table Does not know what I know Does not know what Adina knows Does not know what her room is

The Red Woman believes in something Every person there has used

The Seven want the glory The Riders want the field The priests want the purple woman Removed from what they’ve built The council wants the trade routes That the south has always held

And the Red Woman Believes it is justice

And Adina Keeps the count

[Verse 2 — Adina, cataloguing, saying nothing] She watches Pride stand up She notes the way he phrases it Not: we protect our people But: we claim what we are owed

She watches the head priest She notes the exact moment he mentions the will of the light and his eyes go to the map of the southern trade roads instead of the sky

She watches the council elder argue for the people in the voice he uses when he argues for himself

She has a very good memory

She never writes it down

She does not tell Leara

Because Leara is already going And Leara needs someone who will go with her without conditions

[Pre-Chorus 2] So Adina watches

And she keeps it in the same quiet place she keeps everything

The count The names The exact phrasing That will matter later

When Leara needs to know who stayed because they chose her

And who stayed because the choosing served them

[Chorus] The Red Woman at the table Does not know what I know Does not know what Adina knows Does not know what her room is

The Red Woman believes in something Every person there has used

The Seven want the glory The Riders want the field The priests want the purple woman Removed from what they’ve built The council wants the trade routes That the south has always held

And the Red Woman Believes it is justice

And Adina Keeps the count

[Bridge — the vote, everyone unanimous, and what Adina does] Now is the time Now is the time Now is the time

They say it until it becomes the room

And the Red Woman stands

And she does not need convincing She was already going She has always been going The south is wrong The light must hold The people need the one who will ride

She is not wrong about all of it

That is the worst part

She is not wrong about all of it

And every person in that room who wants something for themselves knows it

That is why they chose her

And Adina stands last

After all of them

Not because she agrees with the vote

Because she agrees with Leara

[Final Chorus] The Red Woman at the table Will ride because she loves Will fight because she believes Will fall in the battle Because the people in that room Needed someone willing to fall and not be them

And the Red Woman will never know What Adina knew In every meeting Every hour Every room

That of all the voices Saying: now is the time

Only one of them Meant it for her

[Outro — Elara watching, the connection landing] She watches Adina Stand

And she thinks: I know a woman like this

I know what it costs to be the one who stays without needing the war to stay for

She thinks: Diana

She thinks: I understand now where you come from
